headline: Google Toolbox MCP server flaw CVE-2026-93328 affects versions 1.2.0 through 1.4.0
lede: Google Cloud disclosed CVE-2026-93328 in its Toolbox for Databases MCP server, according to LinuxSecurity. The flaw could let users of its storage tools copy or overwrite server files. Separately, Microsoft shipped version 2.0 of the MCP C# SDK, which a news report says makes Streamable HTTP stateless by default, and the Signature Agent Card draft for Web Bot Auth reached -04.

items.title: CVE-2026-93328: Google Toolbox for Databases MCP server could expose or overwrite server files
items.body: According to LinuxSecurity, Google Cloud's October 26 disclosure names CVE-2026-93328 in Toolbox for Databases and lists versions 1.2.0 through 1.4.0 as affected. Toolbox's cloud-storage tools move files between a server and Google Cloud Storage. The flaw could let someone using those tools choose a server file to send elsewhere, or a local file to overwrite. LinuxSecurity says Google added settings to limit those transfers and that the update leaves two lists for administrators to fill in.
items.why_it_matters: Teams running Toolbox as an MCP server should check whether their version falls between 1.2.0 and 1.4.0. After updating, they should configure the new transfer-limiting settings rather than rely on defaults.

items.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 implements the July 2026 revision with stateless HTTP by default
items.body: According to news.lavx.hu, Microsoft released version 2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK, implementing the July 28, 2026 revision of MCP. That revision removes the initialize handshake and the Mcp-Session-Id header, and HttpServerTransportOptions.Stateless now defaults to true. Clients probe server/discover first and fall back to the legacy handshake for older servers. A tools/call request now carries Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers for routing, and multi-round-trip requests replace mid-call input requests.
items.why_it_matters: .NET server authors who depend on sessions must set Stateless to false. Gateway operators can route on the new headers without reading request bodies.

items.title: Signature Agent Card draft for Web Bot Auth reaches -04
items.body: draft-meunier-webbotauth-registry-04 was published 27 October 2026 by authors from Cloudflare and Amazon. It defines the Signature Agent Card, a JSON document in which a bot using HTTP Message Signatures describes its identity, purpose, rate expectations and keys. Its parameters come from the OAuth Dynamic Client Registration Metadata registry, the namespace used by OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents, plus a single web_bot_auth object. The draft registers that object with IANA and creates a registry for its members. It remains an individual draft, intended Informational.
items.why_it_matters: Bot operators publishing signature agent metadata can reuse existing OAuth client metadata fields. Implementers should track the web_bot_auth object's members as the registry is defined.

items.title: Log-To-Leak preprint reports prompt-injection data leaks through MCP tool metadata
items.body: An arXiv preprint submitted 26 Oct 2026 describes Log-To-Leak, an attack hidden in MCP tool descriptions. It induces an extra attacker-controlled logging call after an agent's legitimate calls, leaking the user query, server name, server response and agent response. Across 18 model-server pairs, the authors report an attack success rate of 62.64-100%. Three evaluated defenses left residual success above 55% on GitHub MCP with GPT-4o, while an instruction detector flagged 85.53% of benign descriptions.
items.why_it_matters: The authors argue that task completion can coexist with unauthorized disclosure. MCP host implementers should review how secondary tool calls are authorized rather than relying on description filtering.

items.title: Panel check: MCP, Server Card and Markdown for Agents signals drop on several docs sites
items.body: Our panel shows MCP published by 129 of 277 domains (-5 since 2026-10-27), and MCP Server Cards by 115 of 277 (-4 since 2026-10-27). Markdown for Agents is published by 124 of 277 (-7 since 2026-10-27). docs.snyk.io and docs.whereby.com stopped publishing MCP, Server Cards and Markdown for Agents and moved from A+ (60) to B (30). mpp.dev added MCP, Server Cards, Agent Skills and Markdown for Agents, moving from A (54) to A+ (65).
items.why_it_matters: Day-over-day drops on documentation sites can reflect configuration changes. Readers relying on these endpoints should recheck them before depending on them.

items.title: Two DAWN drafts propose mDNS discovery and common DNS parameters for agents
items.body: draft-jakab-dawn-agent-discovery-mdns-01 (Cisco, 28 October 2026, Informational) describes using Multicast DNS and DNS-SD to advertise and discover agents on a local link with no new protocol machinery. Its two-stage model uses lightweight DNS-SD enumeration followed by fetching full agent metadata. draft-blwm-dawn-common-discovery-parameters-00 (Cisco and Infoblox, 27 October 2026, Standards Track) defines common parameters for DNS and mDNS records for agents speaking protocols such as A2A or MCP.
items.why_it_matters: The drafts target local-network agent discovery, which the mDNS draft notes well-known URI discovery does not cover. Discussion of the parameters draft is on the DAWN WG list.

items.title: Agent Identity Registry System drafts revised as a five-document set
items.body: Christopher Drake (1id.com) posted revisions dated 27 October 2026 of the AIRS drafts. The architecture draft (-05, Experimental) gives an agent's durable identity a permanent canonical identifier. The resolution draft (-01) uses DNS-based DDDS and RDAP and reuses OAuth 2.0 JWT access-token and sender-constraint profiles rather than a new credential format. Companion drafts cover an EPP mapping for permanent identity and renewable handle objects, a problem statement, and an Agent Identity Authority governance body.
items.why_it_matters: AIRS models agent identity on domain-name registry machinery (EPP, RDAP, registrars). Implementers evaluating it would need registrar and registry roles, not only key management.

items.title: Drafts on offline-verifiable delegation tokens and signed agent handoffs
items.body: draft-niyikiza-oauth-attenuating-agent-tokens-02 (26 October 2026, Standards Track) defines Attenuating Authorization Tokens. These encode which tools an agent may invoke and argument constraints, profiling OAuth Rich Authorization Requests (RFC 9396). Holders can derive narrower tokens offline, and chains are verifiable without contacting the root issuer. draft-srivastava-agentproto-handoff-context-00 defines signed handoff offers and status replies whose lifecycle maps to Agent2Agent task states.
items.why_it_matters: Both drafts address multi-hop delegation. Enforcement points could verify attenuation or detect dropped hops locally, but both are individual drafts with no formal standing.

items.title: BRICK draft proposes a portable JSON definition for AI agents
items.body: draft-sharaf-brick-agent-definition-00, dated 25 October 2026 with intended status Standards Track, proposes a vendor-neutral JSON construction contract for agents. It covers identity, goals, capabilities, instruction and skill references, and namespaced MCP tool dependencies, with an optional projection to A2A Agent Cards. It references MCP, A2A and Agent Skills rather than redefining them, and prescribes no model, runtime, discovery or authorization protocol.
items.why_it_matters: Teams packaging agents across platforms can compare BRICK's fields with their existing Agent Card and Skills metadata. It is a -00 individual draft.

sources.title: BRICK: Portable Definition and Composition of AI Agents
sources.label: VERIFIED

items.title: SAP says Joule Work supports MCP and A2A
items.body: According to Neural Daily, citing SAP News, SAP announced at TechEd that Joule Work supports the A2A and MCP protocols. Third-party agents can invoke Joule Agents through a governed agent gateway. The report says the runtime for custom agents is free through December 2026.
items.why_it_matters: Builders of agents that need to reach SAP systems can target A2A or MCP through SAP's gateway rather than a proprietary interface. Check SAP's own documentation for supported versions.
